metas.name: Amazon Area
metas.note: The Amazon area is very distinct. It is fairly flat, and contains many of these trees with white bark (Cordia trichotoma), and oil palms.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Bamboo fences
metas.note:
These fences mostly found in the province of Manabí, located along the central-northwest of Ecuador.

*NOTE These fences can be found occasionally in other parts of the country. *
metas.footer: A Complete Guide for Ecuador (doc) by xumakis

metas.name: Banana plantations
metas.note: Banana plantations are most commonly found in the southwestern part of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Cactus
metas.note: Cactus can be seen growing exclusively near the coast between Manta and Salinas.
metas.footer: 'Guide to Ecuador Bollards (and other things)' by Discord (@Conquistadorito)

metas.name: City Streetsigns
metas.note: Street signs differ from city to city - see the graphic.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Corn crops
metas.note:
If you see corn, you're west of the Andes.

The biggest corn production areas are Manabí and Los Ríos, but you can also find corn fields in Guayas and Loja.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: E40 Salinas-Guayaquil
metas.note: The E-40 between Salinas and Guayaquil is one of the only divided highways in Ecuador, and the only one in the dry area near the southwestern coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: E45/smudge
metas.note: There's a faint black smudge on the Google camera lens along the E-45 highway, all the way from Macas up north to Santa Clara.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: E487: One bolt chevron
metas.note: As opposed to a normal Ecuador chevron that has four bolts on each side, the E487 road north from the city of Cumandá has only one bolt in the middle of the chevron.
metas.footer: Youtube: clueless guy explains Ecuador (secret Chevron meta)

metas.name: Esmeraldas Province
metas.note: The province of Esmeraldas can look similar to the Amazon region, but it is significantly hillier.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Exposed Pipe Lines
metas.note: In the northeast of Ecuador you can find metal pipes along some of the roads.
metas.footer: A Complete Guide for Ecuador (doc) by xumakis

metas.name: Extremely Dry Coastal Landscape
metas.note: This extremely dry landscape is only found in the coastal region between Guayaquil and Manta.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Flattest region
metas.note: The flattest region is located around the city of Guayaquil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Gen 4 Appearance
metas.note:
Generation 4 cannot be found in the north-west and in the south-east (never in Esmeraldas).

*NOTE The whole truck is not always visible. *
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Hexagonal tiless
metas.note: In urban areas, you can commonly pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: High/Low Antenna
metas.note:
The Google car antenna has two distinct variations:

The “high” antenna (purple), where the wire around the antenna is entirely above the halfway line of the antenna.

And the “low” antenna (blue) where the majority of the wire is below the halfway point of the line, and there can be a small bit poking up at the very top.

This is most useful when you have the high antenna, since it will always be in the northern half of the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Loja pole
metas.note: Electricity poles with oval, see-through holes are most common in Loja province. They are occasionally found in neighbouring provinces.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Northern Chevron
metas.note: On Northern chevrons, the bolts are positioned closer to the upper and lower edges, whereas on basic Ecuador chevrons, they are aligned closer to the center.
metas.footer: Youtube: clueless guy explains Ecuador (secret Chevron meta)

metas.name: Oil Palms
metas.note:
The vast majority of Ecuador's oil palm plantations are located in the northwest.

Some plantations are also found in the Amazon region.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Orange commercial license plates
metas.note:
In Ecuador, taxis feature orange license plates with red and white stickers on the side *NOTE similar stickers are used in Peru, but without the orange license plate. *

Other commercial vehicles, such as buses and freight vehicles, also use orange license plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Poop Cam
metas.note: Check out this graphic to see where you can find the poop cam in Ecuador.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Regional Polepaint
metas.note: Most are the city flags painted on the poles
metas.footer: A Complete Guide for Ecuador (doc) by xumakis

metas.name: Semi arid area with pine trees
metas.note: The province of Chimborazo is semi-arid, and has an abundance of pine trees.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Southern mountain roads
metas.note:
The southern regions have many winding mountain roads and exposed brownish red dirt.

The central provinces can have similar roads, but the exposed dirt will usually not be found in these areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Taxi letters
metas.note:
Taxis in Ecuador are very common, and the first letter on each taxi can be used to determine the province you are in. The first letter of the taxi and the first letter of the province name are often the same.

NOTE: This letter will also appear as the first letter on ordinary licence plates respectively in each region. Beware that the letter P, as the letter for Pichincha (the region containing Quito), shows up occasionally in several regions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.

metas.name: Thin Aussie bollard
metas.note: “Aussie bollards” have a rectangular reflector on the front. Unlike actual Australian bollards, they are usually round. The most common type is the thin Aussie bollard, which is mostly found in the far south, with some clusters further north.
metas.footer: 'Guide to Ecuador Bollards (and other things)' by Discord (@Conquistadorito)

metas.name: Tree trunk
metas.note: Epic find by @tottenhamwisps: Part of a tree trunk is visible on the boot of the white Gen 4 Google car, spotted on a couple of roads northwest of Ecuador (see attached map).
metas.footer: Found by @tottenhamwisps (Discord)

metas.name: Tree-lined median
metas.note:
A tree-lined median divides E40 across the sections near the town of Guayaquil - see the map.

Note: on rare occasions in other parts of Ecuador.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Volcanic soil
metas.note:
The roads and hills in the province of Cotopaxi feature dark volcanic soil.

The region is often called "Avenue of the Volcanoes".
metas.footer: A Complete Guide for Ecuador (doc) by xumakis

metas.name: Water smudge
metas.note: Visible water smudge on the Google car lens. You can find this on these roads: E30, E382, E20 & E38.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Yellow/Black-Guardrail
metas.note: If you're driving through Guayas, you'll notice the guardrails stand out—they're painted in a distinct black-and-yellow pattern rather than the standard metallic silver or plain yellow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ecuador.
